top3.whyItMatters: No agent framework defends against poisoned tools, so your model choice is the main safeguard.

top3.headline: A 17GB model on a laptop read games from raw neural weights
top3.whyItMatters: Contested frontier-lab claims about reading model weights can now be tested on a laptop.

top3.headline: NVIDIA open-sources a layer that tells agents what your data means
top3.whyItMatters: Agents querying company data need certified metric definitions, and NVIDIA now ships one for free.

items.title: Schools that switch off Google's Gemini lose Google Search too
items.takeaway: Google bundles Search with Gemini for K-12 student accounts; both are off unless admins turn them on.
items.soWhat: Vendors are tying AI to core tools, so check what you lose before opting out.

items.title: A 17GB model on a laptop read games from raw neural weights
items.takeaway: Qwen 3.8 27B named Pac-Man, Pong and Breakout from weights alone, taking about an hour each, and missed Freeway.
items.soWhat: Weight-reading claims can now be checked on a laptop, not only in frontier labs.

items.title: Vercel binds login sessions to devices to stop stolen-cookie attacks
items.takeaway: Device Bound Session Credentials tie vercel.com sessions to the device TPM; Chrome on Mac and Windows only for now.
items.soWhat: Ask your critical vendors whether stolen session cookies still work from another machine.

items.title: Study: agents rewriting their own rules fixed few recurring problems
items.takeaway: Of 7 tests of Matt Pocock's /retro changes where the problem recurred, 2 removed it and 4 did nothing.
items.soWhat: Self-improving agent setups need a test that proves each change helps, or they drift.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources a layer that tells agents what your data means
items.takeaway: Auto Ontology maps enterprise metadata, checks generated SQL against certified definitions and serves agents via MCP.
items.soWhat: Agents answering data questions need shared metric definitions before anyone trusts their numbers.

items.title: spaCy's author says the Astra weight-editing claims are overstated
items.takeaway: Only 3 of 10 experiments worked from raw weights alone; the Qwen math result used Python and ran the model.
items.soWhat: Read the method behind headline AI results before you plan around them.

items.title: Poisoned MCP tools fooled agents in 23% of tests across 12 frameworks
items.takeaway: Across 9,720 tests, resistance depended on the model, from 0.4% to 49.7% attack success; vendors rejected all disclosures.
items.soWhat: Vet every MCP tool your agents load, because the framework will not stop a poisoned one.

items.title: Best AI agent scored 65 of 100 delivering full professional projects
items.takeaway: DeliverBench chains 150 subtasks across 11 projects such as due diligence and contract drafting.
items.soWhat: Agents still need human checkpoints on multi-step professional work where errors compound.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.03412: Best AI agent scored 65 of 100 delivering full professional projects

items.title: Agents break rules after context compaction even when rules survive
items.takeaway: Compacted runs that keep the rule violate it more than twice as often as full-history runs.
items.soWhat: Long-running agents need rules enforced outside the conversation, not just written into it.
